ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r1.claim: The Qur'an also mentions manna and quails in 2:57 and 7:160.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r1.anchor: found in the Qur'an in two other places as well (namely, in 2:57 and 7:160)

ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r2.speaker: Arab philologists
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r2.claim: Mann can mean both the desert plants' sweet resin and anything graciously bestowed without effort by its recipient.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r2.anchor: the term mann denotes not only the sweet, resinous substance exuded by certain plants of the desert, but also everything that is "bestowed as a favour"

ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r3.speaker: Qamus
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r3.claim: Salwa means both quail and whatever comforts people after deprivation.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r3.anchor: the term salwa signifies not merely "a quail" or "quails", but also "all that makes man content and happy after privation" (Qamus)

ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r4.claim: Together, manna and quails metonymically represent sustenance God freely provided to Moses' followers.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n64/r4.anchor: the combination of these two terms denotes, metonymically, the gift of sustenance freely bestowed by God upon the followers of Moses

ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n65/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n65/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n65/r1.claim: The command may also mean not to act arrogantly by attributing God's favors to one's own excellence through descent from Abraham.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n65/r1.anchor: do not attribute these favours to your own supposed excellence on account of your descent from Abraham

ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n66/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n66/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n66/r1.claim: Classical commentators almost unanimously read God's wrath as the unavoidable retribution people bring on themselves by deliberately rejecting guidance and transgressing justice.
ASAD-NOTES:20:80#n66/r1.anchor: almost complete unanimity among the classical commentators in that God's "condemnation" (ghadab, lit., "wrath") is a metonym for the inescapable retribution

ELMALILI:20:77-89/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:77-89/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:77-89/r2.claim: He renders the consequence of divine wrath as falling into an abyss.
ELMALILI:20:77-89/r2.anchor: her kim üzerine de gazabım inerse o uçuruma gider

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.claim: The passage tells everyone to enjoy God's gifts without excess, never despair of mercy despite grave ingratitude, and seek forgiveness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:80/r2.anchor: bütün insanlara, ölçüyü kaçırmadan Allah’ın verdiği nimetlerden yararlanmaları, –yaptıkları nankörlük ne kadar büyük olursa olsun– Allah’ın rahmetinden ümit kesmemeleri gerektiği mesajı verilmekte ve herkes Allah’tan bağışlanma dileğinde bulunmaya çağırılmaktadır.

BURSEVI:v5p315/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315/r1.claim: Ṭayyib means pleasant or lawful; al-Rāghib says legally good food is taken through permissible means, in a permissible amount and place, so it is good now and later.
BURSEVI:v5p315/r1.anchor: قال الراغب : أصل الطيب ما تستلذه الحواس والنفس والطعام الطيب في الشرع

BURSEVI:v5p315/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315/r2.claim: Transgression over provision includes failing to give thanks, waste and arrogance, withholding what is due, and storing more than a day and night.
BURSEVI:v5p315/r2.anchor: الطغيان تجاوز الحد في العصيان أي : ولا تتجاوزا الحد فيما رزقناكم

BURSEVI:v5p315/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315/r3.claim: The consequence clause answers the prohibition: God's anger becomes due as punishment; with kasra yaḥillu means become due, while with ḍamma yaḥullu means descend.
BURSEVI:v5p315/r3.anchor: جواب للنهي أي : فيلزمكم عقوبتي وتجب لكم من حل الدين يحل بالكسر إذا وجب أداؤه

BURSEVI:v5p315/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315/r4.claim: When attributed to God, anger means punishment or vengeance rather than a bodily stirring of the heart.
BURSEVI:v5p315/r4.anchor: والغضب ثوران دم القلب عند إرادة الانتقام وإذا وصف الله تعالى به فالمراد الانتقام دون غيره

BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r1.claim: Whoever incurs God's anger has fallen and perished; the image is a fatal fall from a mountain, and al-Zamakhsharī says following passion leads to its farthest depths.
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r1.anchor: {ومن يحلل عليه غضبى فقد هوى} أي : تردى وهلك وأصله أن يسقط من جبل

BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r2.claim: The Najmiyya reading takes manna as God's attributes and quail as His gracious character; eating the good things means embodying those divine qualities and noble manners.
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : ونزلنا عليهم المن من صفاتنا والسلوى سلوى أخلاقنا

BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r3.claim: Divine care saves spirit and heart from the Pharaoh-like soul, and divine support enables people to take on God's attributes and character.
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r3.anchor: أي : لو لم تكن العناية الربانية لما نجا الروح والقلب وصفاتهما

BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r4.claim: Those who receive divine attributes must not claim lordship or abandon servitude; ecstatic sayings such as I am the Real or Glory be to me can arise from human nature and provoke anger, since states do not establish spiritual stations.
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r4.anchor: فلا تطغوا بأن تدعوا العبودية وتدعوا الربوبية وتسموا باسمي بأن اتصفتم بصفاتي كما قال بعضهم أنا الحق وبعضهم سبحاني وما أشبه هذه الأحوال

BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r5.claim: The warning means that such transgression can make all the servant's devotional dealings come to nothing; therefore God commands the servant to seek guidance.
BURSEVI:v5p315#2/r5.anchor: ولهذا الوعيد أمر الله عباده في الاستهداء بقوله : {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم * صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم}

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads both verbs with ḍamma, in yaḥullu and yaḥlil.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي وحده: (فيحل عليكم) بضم الحاء، (ومن يحلل) بضم اللام.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r2.claim: The other readers use kasra in yaḥillu and the unmarked form yaḥlil.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: فيحل، ومن يحلل عليه.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r3.claim: The root can mean that an affair descends, that someone resides, or that a knot is undone; other forms mean becoming permitted or leaving consecration.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r3.anchor: أبو زيد تقول: قد حل عليه أمر الله يحل حلولا، وحل الدار يحلها حلولا: إذا نزلها، وحل العقدة يحلها حلا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r4.claim: With kasra, yaḥillu evokes becoming lawful; here the anger descends upon and reaches its recipients, as in the Qurʾanic usage of God’s punishment arriving.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r4.anchor: «أنه لشارب حل وبل» أي: مباح له غير محظور عليه، ولا ممنوع منه،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r5.claim: With ḍamma, anger is treated like punishment that descends on someone, since punishment follows and accompanies divine anger.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p242#2/r5.anchor: ووجه من قال: (يحل عليكم غضبي) أن الغضب لما كان يتبعه العقوبة والعذاب

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r2.claim: Both verbs in فيحل عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل are read with kasra or ḍamma: kasra means ‘descended/occurred,’ ḍamma ‘became due’; the author prefers kasra by analogy with the consensus reading ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r2.anchor: فالحجة لمن كسر أنه أراد نزل ووقع والحجة لمن ضم أنه أراد وجب والوجه الكسر لإجماعهم على قوله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r3.claim: The author explains assimilation in فيحل and clarity in ومن يحلل by the movement of the adjacent lām consonants: assimilation requires two moving consonants, while the other pattern retains a still second lām after vowel transfer.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r3.anchor: إنما يكون الإدغام في متحركين فسكن الأول لاجتماعهما ثم يدغم فإن كان الأول متحركا والثاني ساكنا بطل الإدغام

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r4.claim: بملكنا with kasra means ownership, with ḍamma means authority or dominion, and with fatḥa is the verbal noun of ملك يملك.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r4.anchor: فالحجة لمن كسر أنه أراد اسم الشيء المملوك كقولك هذا الغلام ملكي وهذه الجارية ملك يمينى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r5.claim: The ḍamma reading of بملكنا means authority, supported by the verse asking ‘whose is the dominion today?’
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r5.anchor: والحجة لمن ضم أنه أراد بسلطاننا ودليله قوله تعالى ﴿ لمن الملك اليوم ﴾ يريد السلطان

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r6.claim: The fatḥa reading of بملكنا is the verbal noun from ملك يملك.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p245#2/r6.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح أنه أراد المصدر من قولهم ملك يملك ملكا

QIRAAT-ER:20:81:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:5#1/r1.claim: The singular divine “I” replaces the plural of majesty “We,” emphasizing God's personal role in providing sustenance.
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:5#1/r1.anchor: intensifying personal divine agency in provisioning

QIRAAT-ER:20:81:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:11#1/r1.claim: Ḍamma on ḥāʾ yields yaḥulla from ḥ-l-l, meaning to alight or settle, rather than yaḥilla from ḥ-l-y, to descend.

QIRAAT-ER:20:81:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:16#1/r1.claim: Changing the lām vowel likewise distinguishes ḥ-l-l, to settle or alight, from ḥ-l-y, to descend, paralleling the preceding split.
QIRAAT-ER:20:81:16#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift kasra→ḍamma on lām: disambiguates toward ḥ-l-l

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r1.claim: Qatadah explains that God’s wrath will descend upon them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فيحل عليكم غضبي ﴾ قال ينزل عليكم غضبي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r2.claim: Qatadah says Samiri blamed Moses’ delay on their borrowed ornaments, forged a calf from them, used a horse’s hoof-trace to make it low, and claimed it was their and Moses’ god.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال لما استبطأ موسى قومه قال لهم السامري إنما احتبس عنكم من أجل ما عندكم من الحلي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says the horse Gabriel rode embodied life; Samiri took its trace and cast it into the calf, which then lowed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p18#4/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي إن الفرس التي كان عليها جبريل كانت الحياة فقبض السامري من أثرها فلما نبذه في العجل خار

QASHANI:20:80-82/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:80-82/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:80-82/r3.claim: Eating wholesome provisions means feeding the heart with good knowledge and receiving it, since it gives the heart life.
QASHANI:20:80-82/r3.anchor: أي: تغذوا تلك المعارف الطيبة وتقبلوها بقلوبكم فإنها سبب حياتها

QASHANI:20:80-82/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:80-82/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:80-82/r4.claim: Transgression is the ego’s self-display and conceit when it sees its beauty, perfection, and adornment in the light it receives.
QASHANI:20:80-82/r4.anchor: بظهور النفس وإعجابها بنفسها عند استشراقها ورؤيتها بهجتها وكمالها

QASHANI:20:80-82/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:80-82/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:80-82/r5.claim: The resulting wrath is deprivation and abandonment; falling means leaving nearness for the self’s hell and being veiled from the light of beauty.
QASHANI:20:80-82/r5.anchor: { فيحل عليكم } غضب الحرمان وآفة الخذلان { فقد هوى } سقط عن مقام القرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r1.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r1.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads ولا تطغوا with ḍamma on ghayn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r1.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ولا تطغوا فيه بضم الغين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the prohibition as forbidding people to wrong one another by taking provisions unjustly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ولا تطغوا فيه لا يظلم بعضكم بعضا فيأخذه من صاحبه يعني بغير حق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r3.speaker: الضحاك، مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil say it means not to exceed the bounds of what is permitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r3.anchor: وعن الضحاك ومقاتل: لا تجاوزوا حد الإباحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r4.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets it as not rejecting the blessing or using God’s gifts to disobey Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r4.anchor: وعن الكلبي: لا تكفروا النعمة أي لا تستعينوا بنعمتي على مخالفتي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r5.claim: The majority read فيحل and من يحلل with kasra, meaning wrath becomes due and overtakes the transgressor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور فيحل بكسر الحاء ومن يحلل بكسر اللام أي فيجب ويلحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r6.speaker: الكسائي، قتادة، أبو حيوة، الأعمش، طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r6.claim: These readers vocalize the forms with ḍamma, interpreting the threat as God’s wrath descending; Ibn ʿUtayba also has ḍamma in يحلل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r6.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بضم الحاء ولام يحلل أي ينزل وهي قراءة قتادة وأبي حيوة والأعمش وطلحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r7.speaker: ابن غزوان عن طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r7.claim: Ibn Ghazwān reports from Ṭalḥa لا يحلن عليكم غضبي, an admonitory construction against exposing oneself to wrath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r7.anchor: وفي الإقناع لأبي علي الأهوازي ما نصه ابن غزوان عن طلحة لا يحلن عليكم غضبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r8.speaker: قتادة، عبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار، ابن وثاب، الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r8.claim: Al-Lawāmiʿ reports their transitive reading in which Israel’s transgression brings God’s wrath down; alternatively wrath is the subject and punishment is omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r8.anchor: وفي كتاب اللوامح قتادة وعبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وابن وثاب والأعمش فيحل بضم الياء وكسر الحاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r9.claim: هوى euphemistically means destruction: falling from a mountain, falling into calamity after safety, or falling into Hell and divine displeasure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p364/r9.anchor: فقد هوى كنى به عن الهلاك، وأصله أن يسقط من جبل فيهلك

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r5.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r5.claim: “Good” sustenance means provision acquired without disobeying God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r5.anchor: ويقال الطيب من الرزق ما لا يعصي الله مكتسبه

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r6.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r6.claim: “Good” sustenance means provision received while consciously witnessing the Sustainer.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r6.anchor: ويقال الطيب من الرزق ما يكون على مشاهدة الرزاق

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r7.claim: “Good” sustenance means provision that gives rise to gratitude.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r7.anchor: ويقال الطيب من الرزق ما حصل منه الشكر

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r8.claim: God’s elect receive in this life, privately, an early share of the good that others receive openly in the afterlife.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r8.anchor: مؤجل في عقباهم جهرا ، معجل لأصفيائه في دنياهم سرا

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r9.claim: Provision differs by level: the self receives enabling, the heart receives affirmation, and the spirit receives realization.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r9.anchor: فرزق النفوس التوفيق ، ورزق القلوب التصديق

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r10.claim: One meaning of transgressing in provision is crossing from lawful food into unlawful food.

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r11.claim: Another meaning is taking more than the bare minimum needed to survive.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r11.anchor: بالزيادة على الكفاف وما لا بد منه مما زاد على سد الرمق

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r12.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r12.claim: Another meaning is eating heedlessly and forgetfully.

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r13.claim: God’s anger may descend through abandonment after one sin follows another.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r13.anchor: فيحل عليكم غضبي بالخذلان لمتابعة الزلة بعد الزلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r14.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r14.claim: Another explanation is that divine anger comes when people fail to regret what they have lost.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r14.anchor: ويقال فيحل عليكم غضي لفقدكم التأسف على ما فاتكم

QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r15.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r15.claim: Another explanation is that divine anger comes from accepting one’s diminished spiritual state.
QUSHAYRI:v2p267/r15.anchor: ويقال بالرضا بما أنتم فيه من نقصان الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r1.claim: “Good things” means pleasant foods by natural taste or lawful foods by religious law; it can include both qualities, and the command opens a fresh explanation permitting the provision and completing the blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r1.anchor: أي من لذائذه أو حلالاته على أن المراد بالطيب ما يستطيبه الطبع أو الشرع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r2.claim: God mentions rescue first because preventing harm takes precedence over gaining benefit, the religious favor second as nobler, and worldly provision last as lesser.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r2.anchor: وقدم سبحانه نعمة الانجاء من العدو لانها من باب درء المضار وهو أهم من جلب المنافع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r3.claim: “Do not transgress concerning it” forbids ingratitude, violating God's limits through excess or arrogance, using provision for sin, and withholding obligatory dues.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r3.anchor: بالاخلال بشكره وتعدى حدود الله تعالى فيه بالسرف والبطر والاستعانة به على معاصي الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the prohibition as forbidding people to wrong one another by taking another's provision without right; another view says not to store it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما : أي لا يظلم بعضكم بعضا فياخذه من صاحبه بغير حق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads “تطغوا” with a ḍamma on the ghayn.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضى الله تعالى عنهما ( ولا تطغوا ) بضم الغين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r6.claim: “Then My wrath becomes due upon you” answers the prohibition; the verb for a debt becoming due derives from physical arrival or settling, then became conventional for nonphysical matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r6.anchor: جواب للنهى أي فيلزمكم غضبي ويجب لكم من حل الدين يحل بكسر الحاء إذا وجب اداؤه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r7.claim: “He has fallen” means perished; it originally denotes falling from a height, whose ruinous result supplied the metaphor, or specifically falling into the abyss according to al-Zajjāj.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r7.anchor: أي هلك واصله الوقوع من علو كالجبل ثم استعمل في الهلاك للزومه له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r8.claim: An unnamed report describes a palace in Hell where a disbeliever falls from its top for forty years before reaching the bottom, illustrating the original physical sense of “هوى.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r8.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن في جهنم قصرا يرمى الكافر من اعلاه فيهوى في جهنم اربعين خريفا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, Qatāda, Abū Ḥaywa, al-Aʿmash, and Ṭalḥa read “فيحل” with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and “يحلل” with ḍamma on the first lām; Ibn ʿUtba agrees on the latter.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي فيحل بضم الحاء ومن يحلل بضم اللام الأولى وهي قرأءة قتادة وابى حيوة والأعمش وطلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r10.speaker: ابن غزوان عن طلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r10.claim: Ibn Ghazwān, transmitting from Ṭalḥa, reads “لا يحلن عليكم” with emphatic nūn, fatḥa on lām, and kasra on ḥāʾ, on the pattern of a prohibitive “I do not want to see you here.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r10.anchor: قرأ ابن غزوان عن طلحة ( لا يحلن عليكم ) بنون مشددة وفتح اللام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r11.speaker: قتادة وعبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وابن وثاب والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r11.claim: Qatāda, ʿAbd Allāh b. Muslim b. Yasār, Ibn Thāb, and al-Aʿmash read “فيحل” in the causative form; its subject can be transgression with wrath as object, or God with punishment understood as the omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r11.anchor: قرأ قتادة وعبد الله بن مسلم بن يسار وابن وثاب والأعمش فيحل بضم الياء وكسر الحاء من الاحلال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r12.claim: With ḍamma on ḥāʾ, “يحل” means to descend or settle, as in al-Kashshāf.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p239#2/r12.anchor: ومعنى يحل مضموم الحاء ينزل من حل بالبلد إذا نزل كما في الكشاف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r1.claim: Al-Miṣbāḥ allows both “يحل” and “يحل” for punishment, though other forms of “حل” take only kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r1.anchor: وفي المصباح حل العذاب يحل ويحل هذه وحدها بالكسر والضم والباقي بالكسر فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r2.claim: A hadith describes human anger as the heart's blood boiling when vengeance is intended, with swollen veins and reddened eyes; this bodily meaning cannot be intended of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث اتقوا الغضب فانه جمرة توقد في قلب ابن آدم ألم تروا إلى انتفاخ اوداجه وحمرة عينيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r3.claim: Divine wrath means what befits God's majesty: vengeance, punishment, or their willing; al-Alusi seeks refuge from it and says describing it as “حلول” is literal on some readings and figurative on others.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r3.anchor: وإذا وصف الله تعالى به لم يرد هذا المعنى قطعا واريد معنى لاثق بشأنه عز شأنه وقد يراد به الانتقام والعقوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r4.claim: Al-Intiṣāf says “حلول” cannot describe a will of punishment itself; as with the hadith of God's descent, it may be interpreted suitably or name the effect of the will by the will that causes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p240/r4.anchor: وفي الانتصاف أن وصفه بالحلول لا يتأتى على تقدير أن يراد به إرادة العقوبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the prohibition against transgressing as a prohibition on wrongdoing.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says not to disbelieve in the blessing and thereby become transgressors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: لا تكفروا النعمة فتكونوا طاغين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation forbids spending the provision in disobedience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation forbids hoarding the provision, which then becomes wormy if stored.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: لا تدخروا، ثم ادخروا فتدود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.speaker: الأعمش، الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.claim: Al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read both verbs with a damma, meaning God's anger descends; other readers use a kasra, meaning it becomes due.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r5.anchor: قرأ الأعمش، والكسائي: "فيحل" بضم الحاء "ومن يحلل" بضم اللام، أي: ينزل، وقرأ الآخرون بكسرها أي: يجب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p287#2/r6.claim: Whoever incurs God's anger has perished and falls into the Fire.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r5.claim: The good things God provided are either delights or lawful foods.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r6.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the rescue, promise, and provision verbs with first-person singular “I”; other readings include “I promised” and “We promised.”

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.claim: Transgression over provisions means neglecting gratitude or exceeding God's limits through waste, arrogance, or withholding what is due.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r8.anchor: بالإخلال بشكره والتعدي لما حد الله لكم فيه كالسرف والبطر والمنع عن المستحق

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.claim: God's anger becomes binding upon the transgressor, like a debt whose payment has come due.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.anchor: فيلزمكم عذابي ويجب لكم من حل الدين إذا وجب أداؤه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.claim: One gloss says the one reached by God's anger has fallen into the abyss; al-Kisaʾi reads the verbs with ḍamma to mean “descend.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.anchor: وقيل وقع في الهاوية، وقرأ الكسائي «يحل» و { يحلل } بالضم

SULAMI:v1p446#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p446#4/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p446#4/r1.claim: Pure provision is enough to sustain life; excess in food should be avoided because it can intoxicate and distract from remembrance.
SULAMI:v1p446#4/r1.anchor: قال سهل : كلوا من طيبات مما رزقناكم ، كلوا منها القوام وإمساك الرمق فإنه الطيب من الرزق

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r20.claim: The command to eat signals permission, good provision signals abundance, and the phrase what We provided stresses the greatness of the gift.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r20.anchor: ودل على نعمة الإذن فيه بقوله : { كلوا } ودل على سعته بقوله : { من طيبات ما }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r21.claim: Israel must not hoard manna for the next day except before the Sabbath, act arrogantly, neglect gratitude, or spend provision outside obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r21.anchor: بالادخار إلى غد في غير يوم الجمعة ولا بغير ذلك من البطر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r22.claim: The group reading with kasra makes the wrath become due at its proper time, while al-Kisa'i's damma reading conveys a great descent and forceful settling.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r22.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالكسر , ونزولا عظيما وبروكا شديدا - على قراءة الكسائي بالضم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r23.claim: Whoever incurs God's wrath perishes like someone who has fallen from a height.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p33/r23.anchor: أي كان حاله حال من سقط من علو

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p281#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p281#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p281#3/r1.claim: Hawā means perished; the idiom hawat ummuhu means he was destroyed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p281#3/r1.anchor: أي هلك. يقال: هوت أمه. أي هلكت.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the address may target Muhammad’s contemporaries by recalling what God did for their ancestors; then eat is elliptical for it was said to them, and the passage rebukes their ancestors’ ingratitude. The author prefers the first reading as clearer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون هذه المقالة خوطب بها معاصر ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، المعنى هذا فعلنا بأسلافكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r11.claim: Ṭayyibāt here combines the senses of lawful and pleasing or tasty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r11.anchor: وقوله تعالى: من طيبات يريد الحلال الملذ لأن المعنى في هذا الموضع قد جمعهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r12.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r12.claim: Mālik takes ṭayyib in Qurʾānic usage to mean lawful.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r13.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r13.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī takes ṭayyib to mean what people find agreeable; the juristic disagreement concerns repulsive or impure animals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r13.anchor: وقال الشافعي ما يطيب للنفوس، وساق إلى هذا الخلاف تفقههم في الخشاش والمستقذر من الحيوان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r14.claim: To transgress means to exceed the limit and act recklessly, as the Israelites did.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r14.anchor: وتطغوا معناه تتعدون الحد وتتعسفون كالذي فعلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r15.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r15.claim: The majority read fa-yaḥilla and man yaḥlil with kasr, with the first meaning becomes due and the second falls or descends upon him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r15.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «فيحل» بكسر الحاء «ومن يحلل» بكسر اللام، وقرأ الكسائي وحده «فيحل» بضم الحاء «ومن يحلل» بضم اللام فمعنى الأول فيجب ومعنى الثاني فيقع وينزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r16.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r16.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads both forms with ḍamm, giving the sense of falling or descending.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r16.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وحده «فيحل» بضم الحاء «ومن يحلل» بضم اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r17.claim: Hawā means to fall from a height downward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p55#3/r17.anchor: وهوى معناه سقط من علو إلى أسفل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r1.speaker: خنافر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r1.claim: Khinafir’s line uses hawā of a falling eagle; another poet’s line describes a bucket falling as the rope lets it go.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r1.anchor: فهوى هوي العقاب قال القاضي أبو محمد: وإن لم يكن سقوطا فهو شبيه بالساقط والسقوط حقيقة قول الآخر: [الوافر] هوي الدلو أسلمه الرشاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r2.claim: Even if the fall is not literal, someone plunged into disaster after being safe is like a fallen person; here the condemned person falls into Hell and God’s anger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r2.anchor: فالآية من هذا أي «هوي» في جهنم وفي سخط الله،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r3.claim: Another explanation derives the verb from al-hāwiya, the pit of Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p56/r3.anchor: وقيل أخذ الفعل من لفظ الهاوية وهو قعر جهنم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r1.claim: ‘Eat’ means that God told the Israelites to eat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى كلوا أي وقلنا لهم كلوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r2.claim: One explanation of ‘do not transgress with it’ is not to become insolent over blessings and oppress others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r2.anchor: لا تبطروا في نعمي فتظلموا والثاني لا تجحدوا نعمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r3.claim: A second explanation is not to deny God’s blessings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r3.anchor: والثاني لا تجحدوا نعمي فتكونوا طاغين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r4.claim: A third explanation is not to store more than a day and night’s supply.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r4.anchor: والثالث لا تدخروا منه لأكثر من يوم وليلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r5.claim: God’s anger becoming due means His punishment becomes obligatory.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r5.anchor: فيحل عليكم غضبي أي فتحب لكم عقوبتي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r6.claim: Most readers pronounce yaḥill with kasra on ḥāʾ and yaḥlil with kasra on lām.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r6.anchor: والجمهور قرؤوا فيحل بكسر الحاء ومن يحلل بكسر اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r7.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads both forms with ḍamma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي فيحل بضم الحاء ومن يحلل بضم اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r8.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ prefers the kasra: ḍamma means to descend or occur, whereas kasra means become due, matching the explanation of obligation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r8.anchor: قال الفراء والكسر أحب الي لأن الضم من الحلول ومعناه الوقوع ويحل بالكسر يجب وجاء التفسير بالوجوب لا بالوقوع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p311#3/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى فقد هوى أي هلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r5.claim: The Israelites were told not to exceed their need or disobey God's commands in using His provision, lest His anger descend on them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r5.anchor: ولا تطغوا في رزقي، فتأخذوه من غير حاجة، وتخالفوا ما آمركم به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that one on whom God's anger descends has become wretched.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r6.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: أي: فقد شقي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r7.speaker: شفي بن ماتع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r7.claim: Shafi ibn Matiʿ says a disbeliever falls from a high castle in Hell for forty years before reaching the baked clay; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits this as an explanation of falling under wrath.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p308/r7.anchor: وقال شفي بن ماتع: إن في جهنم قصرا يرمى الكافر من أعلاه

JISHUMI:v7p4715/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4715/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4715/r1.claim: The statement that one on whom God's anger descends has fallen means that a grave sinner falls and deserves punishment, against the Murjiʾa.
JISHUMI:v7p4715/r1.anchor: يدل قوله: (ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى) أن الفاسق ممن يهوي ويستحق العقاب خلاف قول المرجئة.

NAHHAS:v3p52/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p52/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p52/r7.claim: Abundance and well-being should not lead them to disobedience; ṭughyān means going beyond what is due.
NAHHAS:v3p52/r7.anchor: أي لا تحملكم السعة والعافية أن تعصوا لأن الطغيان التجاوز إلى ما لا يجب

NAHHAS:v3p52/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p52/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v3p52/r8.claim: Most Kufans read yaḥlil; Arab usage gives yaḥillu for becoming due and yaḥillu for descending.
NAHHAS:v3p52/r8.anchor: وأكثر الكوفيين يقرأ ( يحلل ) حكى أبو عبيدة وغيره أنه يقال حل يحل إذا وجب

NAHHAS:v3p52/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p52/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p52/r9.claim: The kasra reading is preferable because readers agree on the same form in “and a lasting punishment is due upon him.”
NAHHAS:v3p52/r9.anchor: والمعنيان متقاربان إلا أن الكسر أولى لأنهم قد أجمعوا على قوله ﴿ ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

NAHHAS:v3p52/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p52/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p52/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq explains “he has fallen” as having perished and reached the deepest part of Hell.
NAHHAS:v3p52/r10.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق فقد هوى فقد هلك صار إلى الهاوية وهي قعر النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r7.claim: Exceeding the limits of blessings includes denying them, being distracted from gratitude by pleasure, spending on sins, denying the poor their due, extravagance, arrogance, and pride.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r7.anchor: أن يتعدوا حدود الله فيها بأن يكفروها ويشغلهم اللهو والتنعم عن القيام بشكرها ، وأن ينفقوها في المعاصي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r8.claim: A reading has “so it descends,” while ʿAbd Allāh reads “do not let it descend.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r8.anchor: قرىء { فيحل } وعن عبد الله ( لا يحلن )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r9.claim: With kasra, “becomes due” means obligation, as a debt comes due; with ḍamma, it means descending. God's anger is described as descending because it is punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r9.anchor: { ومن يحلل } المكسور في معنى الوجوب ، من حل الدين يحل إذا وجب أداؤه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r10.claim: “He fell” means he perished, originally by falling from a mountain and dying, or by an irrecoverable fall.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r10.anchor: { هوى } هلك . وأصله أن يسقط من جبل فيهلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r11.claim: An Arabic poem illustrates the sense of falling from a mountain and being crushed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p80/r11.anchor: قالت : هوى من رأس مرقبة … ففتت تحتها كبده

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r1.claim: One interpretation of not transgressing concerning the provision is not to disbelieve in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r1.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : لا تكفروا به

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r2.claim: They were forbidden to store the manna for more than a day and night; what they stored became worm-ridden, and otherwise food would never have become worm-ridden.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r2.anchor: لا تدخروا منه لأكثر من يوم وليلة , قال ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the manna they stored became worm-ridden, and without that episode food would never have done so.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r3.anchor: فدود عليهم ما ادخروه , ولولا ذلك ما دود طعام أبدا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r4.claim: A further interpretation is not to use God's provision as aid in disobeying Him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r5.claim: The readings with ḍamma and kasra on the ḥāʾ differ in meaning: the former is to descend, the latter to become due.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r5.anchor: قرىء بضم الحاء وبكسرها ومعناه بالضم ينزل , وبالكسر يجب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r6.claim: The one upon whom God's anger descends has fallen into the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r6.anchor: فقد هوى } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : فقد هوى في النار

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p416/r7.claim: Alternatively, the one upon whom God's anger descends has perished in this world.

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r7.claim: The good provisions mean lawful sustenance, specifically manna and quail, and Israel was forbidden to disobey by saving food for the next day.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r7.anchor: يقول الله تعالى ذكره: { كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم } يعنى بالطيبات الحلال من الرزق { ولا تطغوا فيه }

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r8.claim: Israel disobeyed by storing the food, which became wormy and foul; but for their deed, food would never change.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r8.anchor: وكان الله سبحانه قد نهاهم أن يرفعوا منه لغد فعصوا الله، عز وجل، ورفعوا منه، وقددوا، فتدود ونتن،

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r9.claim: The source adds that, but for Eve, no female would ever betray her husband.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r9.anchor: ولولا حواء زوج آدم، عليهما السلام، لم تخن أنثى زوجها الدهر،

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r10.claim: Transgression here means disobedience, as in God's description of Pharaoh as one who transgressed.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r10.anchor: فذلك قوله: { ولا تطغوا فيه } كقوله تعالى لفرعون: {... إنه طغى } يعنى عصى

MUQATIL:20:80-81/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r11.claim: God's anger means His punishment, and whoever incurs it has perished.
MUQATIL:20:80-81/r11.anchor: { فيحل عليكم غضبي } يعنى فيجب عليكم عذابى { ومن يحلل عليه غضبي } عذابى { فقد هوى }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r2.speaker: كوفي غير عاصم
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r2.claim: Kufan readers except ʿĀṣim read the singular forms for God’s saving, promise, and provision in the preceding address.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r2.anchor: أنجيتكم وواعدتك ورزقتكم كوفي غير عاصم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r3.claim: Transgressing the provision means violating God’s limits by ingratitude and spending it in sins, or wronging one another.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r3.anchor: ولا تتعدوا حدود الله فيه بأن تكفروا النعم وتنفقوها في المعاصي أولا يظلم بعضكم بعضا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r4.claim: God’s wrath is His punishment; whoever incurs it has perished or fallen.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r4.anchor: ﴿ فيحل عليكم غضبي ﴾ عقوبتي ﴿ ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى ﴾ هلك أو سقط سقوطا لا نهوض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r5.speaker: على والباقون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r5.claim: ʿAlī reads the two verbs with fatḥa; the others read both with kasra, where the kasra means becoming due and the ḍamma means descending.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p63#4/r5.anchor: قرا على فيحل ويحلل والباون بكسرهما فالمسكور في معنى الوجوب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.claim: “Good things” means delicious provision; another view takes it as lawful provision, since no human made it and it therefore carried no doubtful human claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r9.anchor: أي من لذيذ الرزق. وقيل: من حلاله إذ لا صنع فيه لآدمي فتدخله شبهة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.claim: Not transgressing in the provision means not letting abundance and well-being lead to disobedience, since transgression is exceeding what is permitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r10.anchor: أي لا تحملنكم السعة والعافية أن تعصوا لأن الطغيان التجاوز إلى ما لا يجوز.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r11.claim: Another view interprets the command as not denying the blessing or forgetting gratitude to the blessing and its giver.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r11.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أي لا تكفروا النعمة ولا تنسوا شكر النعم ولا شكر المنعم بها عليكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r12.claim: Another view says not to exchange the manna and quails for something else, as the Israelites did in the passage about requesting lesser food.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r12.anchor: وقيل: أي ولا تستبدلوا بها شيئا آخر كما قال: أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r13.claim: Do not store more than a day's and night's provision: what they stored became worm-eaten, and without that restriction food would never have spoiled.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فيتدود عليهم ما ادخروه ولولا ذلك ما تدود طعام أبدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r14.claim: The verb “so My wrath descends” is subjunctive after the fa responding to the prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r14.anchor: وهو منصوب بالفاء في جواب النهي من قوله: { ولا تطغوا }.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r15.speaker: الأعمش، يحيى بن وثاب، الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r15.claim: These readers pronounce the ḥāʾ in yaḥillu and the first lām in yaḥlil with ḍamma; the remaining readers use kasra, and both are dialect forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r15.anchor: قرأ الأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب والكسائي «فيحل» بضم الحاء «ومن يحلل» بضم اللام الأولى. والباقون بالكسر وهما لغتان.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r16.speaker: أبو عبيدة، الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r16.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and al-Farraʾ distinguish the readings as “settle/occur” with ḍamma and “become due” with kasra; the meanings are close, but kasra is preferred because 11:39 uses it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:80-81/r16.anchor: أنه يقال: حل يحل إذا وجب وحل يحل إذا نزل. وكذا قال الفراء: الضم من الحلول بمعنى الوقوع والكسر من الوجوب.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r1.claim: God's wrath means His punishment, vengeance, and torment.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r2.claim: “He has fallen” means he has perished, reaching Hell's abyss; the verb can mean falling from a height or dying.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: فقد هلك أي صار إلى الهاوية وهي قعر النار، من هوى يهوي هويا أي سقط من علو إلى سفل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r3.speaker: شفي الأصبحي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r3.claim: A report says Hell contains a mountain named Suʿūd that an unbeliever climbs for forty years, and a palace named Hawā in which he falls for forty years; it links these images to 74:17 and this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:81-82/r3.anchor: عن شفي الأصبحي قال: إن في جهنم جبلا يدعى صعودا يطلع فيه الكافر أربعين خريفا قبل أن يرقاه

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.claim: The account orders blessings by priority: rescue removes harm first, revelation is the greater religious benefit, manna and quails provide worldly benefit, then comes the ban on transgression and assurance that repentance is accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r1.anchor: إزالة المضرة يجب أن تكون متقدمة على إيصال المنفعة ولا شك أن إيصال المنفعة الدينية أعظم في كونه نعمة من إيصال المنفعة الدنيوية

RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the rescue and promise verbs in the second person through the command to eat, except the manna clause, while the other readers use first-person plural throughout.
RAZI-FULL:v22p82#2/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي قد أنجيتكم ووعدتكم إلى قوله : { من طيبات ما رزقناكم } كلها بالتاء إلا قوله : { ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى } فإنها بالنون

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r1.claim: Eat is not an obligatory command but a permission, comparable to the command to hunt after leaving consecration.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r1.anchor: قوله : { كلوا } ليس أمر إيجاب بل أمر إباحة كقوله : { وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا }

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r2.claim: One interpretation of the good things is delicious food, since manna and quails are pleasant foods.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r2.anchor: في الطيبات قولان : أحدهما : اللذائذ لأن المن والسلوى من لذائذ الأطعمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil interpret the good things as lawful food, since God sent it down untouched by human hands; both senses can be combined because they share a common meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r3.anchor: وهو قول الكلبي ومقاتل الحلال لأنه شيء أنزله الله تعالى إليهم ولم تمسه يد الآدميين

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r4.claim: Razi notes that the full discussion of this episode has already appeared in Surat al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r4.anchor: وتمام القول في هذه القصة تقدم في سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets do not transgress as a ban on wronging one another by taking another person’s share.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لا تطغوا ، أي لا يظلم بعضكم بعضا فيأخذه من صاحبه

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r6.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r6.claim: Muqatil and al-Dahhak understand the warning as not wronging oneself by exceeding what permission allows.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل والضحاك : لا تظلموا فيه أنفسكم بأن تتجاوزوا حد الإباحة

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r7.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says not to transgress means not to disbelieve in the blessing, use it to disobey God, neglect gratitude, or trade lawful things for forbidden ones.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي : لا تكفروا النعمة أي لا تستعينوا بنعمتي على مخالفتي ولا تعرضوا على الشكر

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read both forms with ḍamma; al-Aʿmash reports from ʿAbd Allah’s companions a kasra in the first and nominative in the second, while the common reading has kasra in both.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r8.anchor: قرأ الأعمش والكسائي فيحل ومن يحلل كلاهما بالضم وروى الأعمش عن أصحاب عبد الله فيحل بالكسر ومن يحلل بالرفع

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r9.claim: With kasra the verb means that anger becomes due, as in a debt falling due; the ḍamma reading means that it descends upon them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r9.anchor: أما من كسر فمعناه الوجوب من حل الدين يحل إذا وجب أداؤه

RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r10.claim: Fama huwa means he became wretched, or that he fell into the abyss; the verb describes falling from a height downward.
RAZI-FULL:v22p83/r10.anchor: وقوله : { فقد هوى } أي شقي وقيل فقد وقع في الهاوية

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.claim: The Israelites' rescue and manna and quails parallel other passages; the command to eat good provisions is also treated at 2:57.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r1.anchor: For God’s sending down manna and quails to the Israelites and the command to eat of the good things We have provided you

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r2.claim: The warning against exceeding limits joins excess with ingratitude; 2:61 recounts their request for other foods and the response to their ingratitude.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r2.anchor: Exceed not the limits therein is a warning against excess combined with ungratefulness for the blessings that they had been given

STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.claim: The Israelites later ask Moses for an idol like those worshipped by others and worship an idol while he is on Sinai.
STUDYQURAN:20:80/r3.anchor: For the Israelites’ asking Moses to make them an idol similar to the ones they found others worshipping

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r1.claim: The majority reads the verb with kasra on ḥāʾ and lām, from ḥalla meaning to become due; the cited parallels use the same sense.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة من حل عليه كذا أي: وجب، من حل الدين يحل أي: وجب قضاؤه

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r2.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and others read both consonants with ḍamma, deriving the verb from ḥalla meaning to descend.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r2.anchor: وقراءة الكسائي من حل يحل أي: نزل، ومنه

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r3.speaker: ابن عتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUtayba combines the majority’s kasra on ḥāʾ with al-Kisāʾī’s ḍamma on lām.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r3.anchor: وابن عتيبة وافق العامة في الحاء، والكسائي في اللام

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r4.claim: The prevailing analysis makes “My wrath” the subject of yaḥillu in either reading.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r4.anchor: والمشهور أن فاعل " يحل " في القراءتين هو " غضبي "

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r5.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r5.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiḥ treats “My wrath” as an object, with the subject omitted as obvious and understood as their transgression; he disallows making wrath the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r5.anchor: إنه مفعول به، وإن الفاعل ترك لشهرته، والتقدير: فيحل عليكم طغيانكم غضبي

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r6.claim: The author says al-Lawāmiḥ’s account is awkward: if the verb is from iḥlāl, it takes one object, either “My wrath” with transgression as subject or an omitted object with wrath as subject.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r6.anchor: فعنده أن حل متعد بنفسه لأنه من الإحلال كما صرح هو به

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r7.speaker: طلحة
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r7.claim: Ṭalḥa reads a prohibitive lā with emphatic nūn: do not expose yourselves to transgression lest wrath become due, like lā arīnnaka hāhunā.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r7.anchor: وقرأ طلحة " لا يحلن عليكم " ب " لا " الناهية وكسر الحاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r8.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads taṭghaw with ḍamma on ghayn, from ṭaghā yaṭghū, like ghadā yaghdū.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " ولا تطغوا " بضم الغين من طغا يطغوا

SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows yaḥillu to be jussive, coordinated with lā taṭghaw; the author objects that this would wrongly make the verse forbid wrath from descending.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مجزوما عطفا على " لا تطغوا " كذا قال أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r2.claim: The author prefers an accusative subjunctive with an elided an in the consequence clause, which fits the meaning clearly.
SAMIN-DURR:20:81#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب بإضمار " أن " في الجواب. وهو واضح

TAB-FULL:v16p125/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p125/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p125/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the prohibition on transgressing over the provisions as not wronging one another.
TAB-FULL:v16p125/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قول: {ولا تطغوا فيه} [طه: 81] يقول: ولا تظلموا

TAB-FULL:v16p126/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r1.claim: Qatāda explains God’s wrath as descending; the segment gives this as the consequence warned about for disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فيحل عليكم غضبي} [طه: 81] يقول: فينزل عليكم غضبي

TAB-FULL:v16p126/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r2.speaker: قراء الحجاز والمدينة والبصرة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r2.claim: Most readers use the kasra form, which they understand as God's wrath becoming due upon the people.
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r2.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء الحجاز والمدينة والبصرة والكوفة {فيحل عليكم} [طه: 81] بكسر الحاء {ومن يحلل} [طه: 81] بكسر اللام

TAB-FULL:v16p126/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r3.speaker: جماعة من أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r3.claim: A Kufan group uses the ḍamma form, understood as God's wrath falling or descending upon them.
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r3.anchor: وقرأ ذلك جماعة من أهل الكوفة: (فيحل عليكم) بضم الحاء، ووجهوا تأويله إلى ما ذكرنا عن قتادة

TAB-FULL:v16p126/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r4.claim: Both famous readings are correct: Israel was warned both that wrath would descend through disobedience and that it would become due to them.
TAB-FULL:v16p126/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان قد قرأ بكل واحدة منهما علماء من القراء

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r4.claim: The command to eat the good provisions is permissive in force; the phrase good things of what We provided is an adjective joined to its noun, since God's provision is not divided into good and non-good, as another verse confirms.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r4.anchor: إباحة في صورة الأمر وإضافه الطيبات إلى { ما رزقناكم } من إضافة الصفه إلى الموصوف

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r5.claim: Transgression in consuming the provision means ingratitude and failure to give thanks, illustrated by Israel's complaint about having only one food.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r5.anchor: وذلك بكفران النعمة وعدم أداء شكره كما قالوا

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r6.claim: God's anger becoming due is expressed by a verb also used of a debt becoming payable; divine anger is an active attribute realized by willing harm through causes arranged after a servant's disobedience.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r6.anchor: أي يجب غضبي ويلزم من حل الدين يحل من باب ضرب إذا وجب أداؤه والغضب من صفاته تعالى الفعلية

TABATABAI:20:80-82/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r7.claim: The one upon whom God's anger settles has fallen, from the word for falling, and this is interpreted as destruction.
TABATABAI:20:80-82/r7.anchor: أي سقط من الهوي بمعنى السقوط وفسر بالهلاك

TABRISI:20:80/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80/r10.claim: Al-Kisai reads يحل with damma on ح; other readers use kasra in both places.
TABRISI:20:80/r10.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي فيحل بضم الحاء من يحلل بضم اللام والباقون بالكسر في الموضعين

TABRISI:20:80/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80/r11.claim: The kasra reading evokes what is permissible or unrestrained; the phrase describes wrath descending after having been withheld.
TABRISI:20:80/r11.anchor: فمعنى يحل عليكم ينزل بكم وينالكم بعدما كان ذا حظر وحجر ومنع عنكم

TABRISI:20:80/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:80/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:80/r12.claim: The damma reading treats wrath as punishment befalling people, since punishment follows wrath.
TABRISI:20:80/r12.anchor: لما كان تتبعه العقوبة والعذاب جعله بمنزلة العذاب فقال يحل أي ينزل

TABRISI:20:81-85/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:81-85/r1.claim: The imperative to eat good provisions functions as permission.
TABRISI:20:81-85/r1.anchor: صورته صورة الأمر والمراد به الإباحة

TABRISI:20:81-85/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:81-85/r2.claim: One explanation of transgressing in the provision is consuming it in a forbidden way.
TABRISI:20:81-85/r2.anchor: أي فلا تتعدوا فيه فتأكلوه على الوجه المحرم عليكم

TABRISI:20:81-85/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:81-85/r3.claim: Another explanation is not to cross from permitted food into forbidden food.
TABRISI:20:81-85/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن المعنى لا تتجاوزوا عن الحلال إلى الحرام

TABRISI:20:81-85/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:81-85/r4.claim: A third explanation forbids using lawful provision to aid disobedience.
TABRISI:20:81-85/r4.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا تتناولوا من الحلال للاستعانة به على المعصية

TABRISI:20:81-85/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:81-85/r5.claim: On the standard reading, God's wrath becoming due means His punishment is incumbent on them.

TABRISI:20:81-85/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:81-85/r6.claim: With damma on ح, the phrase means that God's punishment descends upon them.
TABRISI:20:81-85/r6.anchor: ومن ضم الحاء فالمعنى فينزل عليكم عقوبتي

TABRISI:20:81-85/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:81-85/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:81-85/r7.claim: Whoever falls from a height has perished, hence the warning that the one reached by wrath has fallen; another view says he falls into Hell, and al-Zajjaj says he reaches the Abyss.
TABRISI:20:81-85/r7.anchor: أي هلك لأن من هوى من علو إلى أسفل فقد هلك

THALABI:v6p256/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p256/r3.claim: Ṭayyibāt means the lawful, wholesome portion of what God provided.
THALABI:v6p256/r3.anchor: كلوا من طيبات حلال ما رزقناكم.

THALABI:v6p256/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p256/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets transgressing the provision as doing wrong.

THALABI:v6p256/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r5.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p256/r5.claim: Muqatil interprets transgressing it as disobeying God.

THALABI:v6p256/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p256/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets transgressing it as being ungrateful for the blessing.

THALABI:v6p256/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p256/r7.claim: Other interpretations say it means forbidding lawful food, spending in disobedience, storing provisions, or using God's blessings to gain strength for disobedience.
THALABI:v6p256/r7.anchor: وقيل: ولا تحرموا الحلال، وقيل: ولا تنفقوا في معصيتي، وقيل: ولا تدخروا، وقيل: ولا تتقووا بنعمي على معاصي.

THALABI:v6p256/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p256/r8.claim: The verb yahillu means that God's wrath becomes due upon them.
THALABI:v6p256/r8.anchor: فيحل يجب عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل يجب عليه غضبي

THALABI:v6p256/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش والكسائي
THALABI:v6p256/r9.claim: They read both verbs with ḍamma on ḥāʾ and lām, giving the sense of descending or alighting.
THALABI:v6p256/r9.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش والكسائي: فيحل ومن يحلل بضم الحاء واللام أي ينزل.

THALABI:v6p256/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p256/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p256/r10.claim: Hawā means he perished and fell into the Fire.
THALABI:v6p256/r10.anchor: فقد هوى هلك وتردى في النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r1.claim: God’s words ‘eat of the good things We provided’ are spoken as a reminder of blessings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {كلوا} أي: وقلنا لهم كلوا {من طيبات ما رزقناكم} وهذا أمر يقتضي التعديد بالنعم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r2.claim: In al-Walibi’s narration, Ibn Abbas glosses ‘do not transgress in it’ as ‘do not do wrong.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي: (يقول لا تظلموا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r3.claim: Muqatil interprets the prohibition as ‘do not disobey.’

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r4.claim: The prohibition means not becoming insolent over the blessing and thereby wronging others; another gloss says not to use God’s gifts as strength for disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r4.anchor: والمعنى لا تبطروا فيما أنعمت عليكم فتظالموا. وهذا المعنى قول من قال: (لا تتقووا بنعمي على معاصي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says they must not deny God’s blessing in what He provided, which would make them transgressors.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (لا تجحدوا نعمة الله فيما رزقكم منه فتكونوا طاغين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r6.claim: Muqatil says they must not exceed the limit with manna and quail by taking more than needed and storing it; storing any of it counts as transgression.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (لا تتعدوا ما حد الله لكم في المن والسلوى فتتجاوزوا قدر ما يكفيكم وتدخروا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r7.claim: Qatada and others take fa-yaḥilla as ‘becomes due.’

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r8.claim: Both kasra and ḍamma readings are transmitted for yaḥilla and yaḥlil.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r9.claim: Al-Farra prefers kasra because it means ‘becomes due,’ matching the explanatory gloss of obligation rather than descent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: (والكسر أحب إلي من الضم؛ لأن الضم من الحلول بمعنى الوقوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r10.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says kasra means ‘becomes due’ while ḍamma means ‘comes down.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ({فيحل عليكم} معناه فيجب عليكم، ومن قرأ: بالضم، فمعناه التنزيل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r11.claim: The readings are close in meaning: with kasra, the ban and protection lift after transgression, so punishment comes upon them; ‘becomes due’ conveys this sense rather than literally defining the word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r11.anchor: فمعنى يحل عليكم: ينزل بكم وينالكم بعدما كان ذا حظر وحجر ومنع عنكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r12.claim: The author supports kasra by 11:39 and by the kasra reading in 20:86; with ḍamma, anger is treated as the punishment that follows it and thus as something descending.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p482/r12.anchor: {ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم} [هود: 39]، أي: ينزل به بعد أن لم يكن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r1.claim: Hawā can mean falling from a height, an eagle swooping on prey, landing in a place, or dying; the author cites lines by al-Nābigha and Kaʿb ibn Saʿd for the sense ‘perished.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r1.anchor: يقال: هوى يهوي هويا: إذا سقط من علو إلى أسفل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r2.speaker: النابغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r2.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line uses hawā for Ziyad’s death or ruin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r2.anchor: قال النابغة (¬2): وقال الشامتون هوى زياد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r3.speaker: كعب بن سعد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r3.claim: Kaʿb ibn Saʿd’s line ‘his mother perished’ illustrates hawā meaning ‘died.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r3.anchor: قول كعب بن سعد (¬3) (¬4): هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح غاديا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r4.claim: One interpretation is that the person perished; another is that he fell into the abyss called al-Hāwiya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r4.anchor: فأما التفسير فقيل: (هلك) (¬1). وقيل: (صار إلى الهاوية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r5.claim: In al-Walibi’s narration, Ibn Abbas explains ‘he has fallen’ as ‘he has become wretched.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p484/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي: (يقول: فقد شقي)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:81-82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:81-82/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:81-82/r1.claim: The Israelites were told to eat lawful provisions and not transgress by showing ingratitude for the blessing; God's anger then becomes due, and whoever incurs it perishes in the abyss.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:81-82/r1.anchor: حلالات { ما رزقناكم ولا تطغوا } ولا تكفروا النعمة { فيه فيحل } فيجب { عليكم غضبي ومن يحلل } [يجب]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r8.claim: The good provisions the Israelites were told to eat were manna and quail.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r8.anchor: قوله: {كلوا من طيبات ما رزقناكم} [طه: 81] المن والسلوى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r9.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says the provisions were lawful food, namely manna and quail.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269/r9.anchor: وقال السدي: {من طيبات ما رزقناكم} [طه: 81] يعني من الحلال، المن والسلوى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r1.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi explains the prohibition on excess as a command not to disobey God in storing or gathering the manna and quail.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r1.anchor: تفسير السدي يعني: لا تعصوا الله في رفع المن والسلوى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r2.claim: Qatada says manna spoiled if kept overnight, except before the Sabbath, when Israelites gathered enough for Friday and Saturday because they did not work on the Sabbath.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r2.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: كانوا لا يأخذون منه لغد، لأنه كان يفسد عندهم ولا يبقى إلا يوم الجمعة فإنهم كانوا يأخذون ليوم الجمعة والسبت

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says that, had the Israelites not stored provisions for the next day after being told to gather only for that day, meat and food would not have spoiled.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لولا بنو إسرائيل ما خنز لحم، ولا أنتن طعام، إنهم لما أمروا أن يأخذوا ليومهم ادخروا من يومهم لغدهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report says meat would not have spoiled without the Israelites and no woman would have betrayed her husband without Eve; part of the food phrase is broken in the source.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لولا بنو إسرائيل ما خنز لحم، ولم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r5.claim: Qatada interprets God's wrath becoming due as His wrath becoming obligatory upon them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: يعني فيجب عليكم غضبي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r6.claim: An alternate reading understands the wrath as descending upon them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p269#2/r6.anchor: وهي تقرأ على وجه آخر: فيحل عليكم غضبي أي: فينزل عليكم غضبي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r1.claim: Qatada explains the alternate form as meaning that God's wrath descends upon the person it overtakes.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r1.anchor: إلا أن قتادة قال: ومن ينزل عليه غضبي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r2.claim: The one upon whom wrath falls has fallen into the Fire.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p270/r3.claim: Al-Suddi explains the one who has fallen as having perished.

BURHAN:v1p284/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p284/r2.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v1p284/r2.claim: Ibn Malik says the Qur’an is mostly in the Hijazi dialect, with a few Tamimi forms: assimilation is Tamimi, while preserving doubled consonants, as in فليملل and يحلل, is common in Hijaz.
BURHAN:v1p284/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك أنزل الله القرآن بلغة الحجازيين إلا قليلا فإنه نزل بلغة التميميين

ITQAN:v4p486/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p486/r1.claim: A report stopped at Ibn Masʿud says every Qur’anic letter has a boundary and every boundary an opening or point of access.
ITQAN:v4p486/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود موقوفا ( إن هذا القرآن ليس منه حرف إلا له حد ولكل حد مطلع )

ITQAN:v4p486/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p486/r2.claim: One interpretation of the Qur’an’s outer and inner aspects is that probing its inner sense and comparing it with its wording reveals its meaning.
ITQAN:v4p486/r2.anchor: أنك إذا بحثت عن باطنها وقسته على ظاهرها وقفت على معناها

ITQAN:v4p486/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p486/r3.claim: Another report says each verse has already been acted on by some people and will be acted on by others later.
ITQAN:v4p486/r3.anchor: أن ما من آية إلا عمل بها قوم ولها قوم سيعملون بها كما قال ابن مسعود

ITQAN:v4p486/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p486/r4.claim: A further explanation identifies the outer aspect with the wording and the inner aspect with its interpretation.

ITQAN:v4p486/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
ITQAN:v4p486/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayd considers this explanation most sound: historical stories outwardly report earlier peoples’ destruction, while inwardly warning later generations not to repeat their deeds.
ITQAN:v4p486/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيد وهو أشبهها بالصواب إن القصص التي قصها الله تعالى عن الأمم الماضية

ITQAN:v4p486/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r6.speaker: ابن النقيب
ITQAN:v4p486/r6.claim: Ibn al-Naqib says the outer sense is what scholars of exoteric learning understand, while the inner sense contains secrets God disclosed to people of spiritual realization.
ITQAN:v4p486/r6.anchor: إن ظهرها ما ظهر من معانيها لأهل العلم بالظاهر وبطنها ما تضمنته من الأسرار

ITQAN:v4p486/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p486/r7.claim: The boundary of a passage is the limit of the meaning God intends; another view makes it the measure of reward or punishment due for a ruling.
ITQAN:v4p486/r7.anchor: ومعنى قوله ( ولكل حرف حد ) أي منتهى فيما أراد الله من معناه

ITQAN:v4p486/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p486/r8.claim: An opening is a route to understanding an obscure meaning or ruling; alternatively, it is where its deserved reward or punishment is disclosed in the afterlife.
ITQAN:v4p486/r8.anchor: لكل غامض من المعاني والأحكام مطلع يتوصل به إلى معرفته

ITQAN:v4p486/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p486/r9.claim: Another formulation calls the outer aspect recitation, the inner aspect understanding, the boundary the rulings of lawful and unlawful acts, and the opening insight into promise and warning.
ITQAN:v4p486/r9.anchor: الظاهر التلاوة والباطن الفهم والحد أحكام الحلال والحرام

ITQAN:v4p486/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p486/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn ʿAbbas saying the Qur’an has many branches, outer and inner dimensions, and inexhaustible wonders; its outer aspect is recitation and inner aspect interpretation, so one should study with scholars and avoid fools.
ITQAN:v4p486/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال إن القرآن ذو شجون وفنون وظهور وبطون لا تنقضي عجائبه

ITQAN:v4p486/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p486/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ITQAN:v4p486/r11.claim: Ibn Sabʿ cites Abu al-Dardaʾ: a person has not fully understood until he recognizes multiple facets in the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v4p486/r11.anchor: ورد عن أبي الدرداء أنه قال لا يفقه الرجل كل الفقه حتى يجعل للقرآن وجوها

ITQAN:v2p320/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r11.claim: “Do not transgress” means “do not act unjustly.”

ITQAN:v2p320/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r12.claim: “He has fallen” means he has become wretched.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r1.claim: Ellipsis can create a subtle grace that disappears when the omitted element is restored aloud; the listener is drawn to keep the omission unspoken.
