JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r1.anchor: ثم تكلف أن ترد ما حذف الشاعر ، وأن تخرجه إلى لفظك ، وتوقعه في سمعك ؛ فإنك تعلم أن الذي قلت كما قلت ،

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r2.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr’s line, هو is omitted before داسع نفسه; the construction’s shape makes the listener avoid mentally restoring that subject.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r2.anchor: الأصل حتى قلت : هو داسع نفسه . أي حسبته من شدة التثاؤب ، ومما به من الجهد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r3.claim: Bakr ibn al-Naṭṭāḥ’s غضبى omits هي (either before or after the adjective); saying the omitted pronoun aloud would destroy the line’s charm.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p125/r3.anchor: والمقصود قوله : ' غضبى ' ، وذلك أن التقدير ' هي غضبى ' أو ' غضبى هي ' لا محالة ،

DAMGHANI:v1p477/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r14.claim: Hawā can mean perish: one on whom God's wrath descends has perished.
DAMGHANI:v1p477/r14.anchor: ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى يعني فقد هلك

DAMGHANI:v1p141/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p141/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p141/r8.claim: Yaḥillu can mean become obligatory or fall due: God's anger becomes due upon those who transgress.
DAMGHANI:v1p141/r8.anchor: يحل بمعنى يجب قوله تعالى في سورة طه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r1.claim: Hawā means to fall; Ibn Fāris cites the verb hawā yahwī and related nouns for a pit or sequential falling.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r1.anchor: هوى : بمعنى سقط . قال ابن فارس : يقال : هوى الشيء يهوي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r2.claim: Al-hāwiya is both a name for Hell and a general term for a deep pit; hawwā means descending, while hawat ummuhu is an insult.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r2.anchor: والهاوية : اسم من أسماء جهنم . والهاوية أيضا : كل مهواة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r4.claim: In the warning about God’s anger, hawā means perished.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p637#2/r4.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى هلك . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.claim: These readers use three first-person plural forms with nūn and alif; Hamza and al-Kisāʾī use tāʾ without alif. Abu ʿAmr alone omits alif in وعدناكم throughout.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r9.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم الثلاثة الأحرف بالنون والألف وقرأ حمزة والكسائى بالتاء بغير ألف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r10.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone dammas ḥāʾ in فيحل and lām in ومن يحلل; others kasra both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p421/r10.anchor: فقرأ الكسائى وحده ﴿ فيحل عليكم ﴾ بضم الحاء ﴿ ومن يحلل ﴾ بضم اللام

NASHR:v2p321/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p321/r1.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p321/r1.claim: Al-Kisai reads the ḥāʾ and lām of both verbs with ḍamma.
NASHR:v2p321/r1.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي بضم الحاء من (فيحل) واللام من (يحلل)

NASHR:v2p321/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p321/r2.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p321/r2.claim: The remaining readers read the ḥāʾ and lām of both verbs with kasra.
NASHR:v2p321/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بكسر الحاء واللام منهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r1.claim: Explaining a verse's occasion, circumstances, and story is permissible only through verified transmitted reports and hearing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r1.anchor: أما التفسير: وهو الكلام في أسباب نزول الآية وشأنها وقصتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r2.claim: Tafsīr derives from tafsira, the water sample a physician examines to uncover a patient's illness; a commentator similarly uncovers a verse's circumstances and story.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r2.anchor: وأصل التفسير من التفسرة وهي: الدليل من الماء الذي ينظر فيه الطبيب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r3.claim: Taʾwīl derives from awwal, return: to make something return or turn it so that it returns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r3.anchor: واشتقاق التأويل من الأول وهو الرجوع. يقال: أولته فآل أي: صرفته فانصرف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r4.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd says the Qur'an came in seven aḥruf, and every verse has an outer and inner aspect, a limit, and a point of ascent; another wording gives every letter a limit and every limit an ascent. No grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف، لكل آية منها ظهر وبطن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r5.claim: One explanation takes the outer aspect as Qur'anic wording and the inner aspect as its interpretation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r5.anchor: قيل: الظهر لفظ القرآن والبطن تأويله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r6.claim: Another explanation says the outer aspect reports how earlier peoples disobeyed and were punished, while its inner lesson warns readers not to repeat their acts and suffer the same fate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r6.anchor: وقيل: الظهر ما حدث عن أقوام أنهم عصوا فعوقبوا فهو في الظاهر خبر وباطنه عظة وتحذير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r7.claim: A third view interprets outer and inner as recitation and understanding: recitation is reading as revealed, while the inner aspect is reflection and contemplation, linked to 73:4 and 38:29.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r7.anchor: وقيل معنى الظهر والبطن: التلاوة والتفهم، يقول: لكل آية ظاهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r8.claim: Recitation is gained through learning and memorization by study; understanding is gained through sincere intention, reverence, and a sound inward disposition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r8.anchor: ثم التلاوة تكون بالتعلم والحفظ بالدرس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r9.claim: Every letter has a boundary in recitation and interpretation: recitation must not go beyond the written Qur'an, and interpretation must not exceed what has been transmitted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r9.anchor: ففي التلاوة لا يجاوز المصحف، وفي التفسير لا يجاوز المسموع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r10.claim: A maṭlaʿ is an ascent toward knowledge of a subject, and can mean understanding; God may open interpretive meanings to contemplative readers that others do not receive.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p46/r10.anchor: وقد يفتح الله على المدبر والمتفكر في التأويل والمعاني ما لا يفتح على غيره،
